# Speed of sound of a mixture

`eos.sound_speed`

## Source

**NeqSim thermo/phase/PhaseEos.java**

Its `getSoundSpeed`: `bs = -(1/V) Cv/Cp / dPdVTn`, `sqrt(V/Mw/bs)`, with the derivative analytic in the cubic's Helmholtz residual; and `SystemThermo.getSoundSpeed`'s beta-weighted sum.


## What this model is

A **direct** model: a computation over vectors, with no iteration and therefore no algorithm block. It is here because a calculation's inputs are scalars, so a composition vector has nowhere in the calc registry to go - and it is a model rather than a library function so that it goes through the spec-driven pipeline like everything else.

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `components` | - | the substances the mixture is made of, by name, resolved against the component databank. |
| `T` | K | the state's absolute temperature. |
| `P` | Pa | the state's absolute pressure. |
| `z` | dimensionless | the mixture's mole fractions, checked rather than renormalised. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sound_speed` | m/s | the speed of sound in the phase the flash puts first - the gas where two phases - at the flashed state, m/s. |
| `system_sound_speed` | m/s | `SystemThermo.getSoundSpeed()`: the beta-weighted mean of the phase speeds. Equal to `sound_speed` on a flashed single phase; a weighted mean, not a mixture speed, on two. |
| `phase` | all_vapour / all_liquid / two_phase / trivial | what the flash found at the state, which says whether the two speeds above differ. |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature |
| `P > 0` | raises | an absolute pressure |

## Assumptions

- **the speed is the cubic's own isentrope.** `c^2 = -gamma (v^2/M) (dP/dv)_T` with `gamma = cp/cv`, `v` the phase's molar volume and `M` its molar mass; `(dP/dv)_T` and `(dP/dT)_v` are closed forms of the same residual the departure functions use.
- **`cp - cv = -T (dP/dT)^2_v / (dP/dv)_T`**, the standard identity, so `cv` needs no separate departure term; `cp` is `eos.molar_enthalpy_entropy`'s at the same composition and root.
- **the phase composition and root are the flash's.** A single-phase feed is read at its own composition; a two-phase feed reads each phase at its own composition and root, which is what a phase sound speed is.
- **the system value is the beta-weighted arithmetic mean** of the phase speeds. NeqSim's own `getSoundSpeed()` sums beta times the phase value; on a two-phase state that mean is not a physical mixture speed and is reported as the class's reading, not as physics.
- **an unflashed NeqSim system doubles the system value**, because two phase objects carry `beta = 1.0` each. Every row here flashes first; the port reports the flashed value and does not reproduce the artefact.
- **the mixture is PR with the classic mixing rule**, because the databank's `mixture_of` has no other route here; SRK and RK share the same `PhaseEos` formula.
- **`PhaseGE`'s constant 1470 m/s and `PhaseDefault`'s NaN are not models** and have no row here; `EquilibriumSoundSpeed`, the re-flash derivative, is `eos.equilibrium_sound_speed`.

## How far this is checked
**`partially_verified`** — exercised against expectations pinned in its own spec, with no independent oracle recorded for it - **the normal case rather than a defect**.

- Tests: 5 declared, every one run
- External check: no external validation case names it

The same account travels with every result this returns: `result.provenance`
carries the status, the spec and both kernels with a SHA-256 of each, and which
declared checks *that call* could not evaluate.
